integrity_admission.policy: All manifest-listed runtime payload and support files are SHA-256 verified before first use. A stamp binds the manifest digest, expected digests, and device/inode/size/mtime/ctime identities. Unchanged identities take the cached path; any stale or missing stamp causes a complete rehash. The experts.pack identity is checked after every prefill chunk and before each output token is published.
integrity_admission.threat_model_limit: The local manifest and stamp are not signed. This detects accidental corruption and ordinary file replacement; it is not an authenticity mechanism against an attacker able to rewrite the artifact, manifest, and stamp together. --force always rehashes payloads against the current manifest.

decision.status: Initial fail-closed runtime reliability gate passed
decision.reason: The real artifact now has automatic whole-artifact admission without token-critical-path checksums. Corruption and in-session replacement stop output; short reads and insufficient capacity raise; failed speculation falls back to the exact demand read; unsafe MLX memory requests are rejected before prefill. The integrated real-artifact guard reproduced the known exact token sequence without swap growth.
decision.quality_scope: These checks show that failure handling cannot silently substitute, skip, remap, truncate, or execute the wrong expert. They do not compare the pinned 4-bit checkpoint with BF16 and do not claim adversarial artifact authenticity.
